subject: Liveframe suppression during demo — customers seeing token stream cutouts (urgent)
messages:
From: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@avenirhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevOps Team <ops@avenirhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live inference interruptions during demo — urgent

Sergio —

We were in the middle of a paid pilot demo with three product stakeholders when the live transcript feed started dropping tokens repeatedly. The UI showed the WebSocket as connected but the generated tokens stopped mid-sentence for ~8–12s, then resumed with a large batch of tokens. We saw both:
- intermittent long pauses (8–20s) where no tokens arrive, then a burst, and
- occasional 502s in the client console tied to chunked transfer errors.

This happened twice during a 40-minute session and the stakeholders asked whether your hosted endpoint is suitable for our real-time summarization use case. They are already nervous about latency. We need an explanation and immediate mitigation — demo at-risk and renewal conversation scheduled next week.

Logs attached: we captured a session recording and a WebSocket trace. Please advise next steps and whether we should move to a non-streaming fallback for the remainder of our trial.

Thanks,
Alyssa Park
Senior PM, Avenir Health

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@avenirhealth.com>
Cc: DevOps Team <ops@avenirhealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live inference interruptions during demo — urgent

Alyssa — thanks for the quick flag and for sending the traces. I’m really sorry you hit this in front of stakeholders. I’ve looped in our real-time reliability and ops leads (Hannah, Markus, Grace, Jordan) to investigate immediately.

Immediate suggestions while we triage:
- If you can, switch the client to the non-streaming generate endpoint (no chunking) — that will trade latency for completeness and avoid the chunked-transfer path.
- If you prefer to stay streaming, reduce concurrency to 1 connection per browser tab temporarily.

We’ll review the attached traces and get back in 45–60m with findings and a mitigation plan. If you’d like an emergency Zoom with the customer ops team, we can set that up now.

— Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Live inference interruptions during demo — traces attached

Forwarding Alyssa's traces — I pulled server-side sampling for their account for the time window and I'm seeing repeated partial chunk writes from the gateway layer to the backend GPUs at ~09:20–09:28 PDT. Summary notes:
- Multiple requests show token throughput halting for ~10s followed by 30–60 token catch-up bursts.
- WebSocket ping/pong looks healthy at the proxy level (no tcp resets) — issue appears after proxy -> runtime handoff.
- A small subset of requests hit the per-customer concurrency threshold and were routed to the fallback queue; we saw automatic model-variant fallback for 3 connections.

Attaching: avenir-ws-trace-0729.json and server sampling slice. I’ll run a deeper trace through the kernel selection logs and KV-cache metrics.

Hannah
SRE, Real-time Runtime

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Live inference interruptions during demo — traces attached

Quick findings from runtime traces (first pass):
- Observed KV-cache eviction storms coincident with the pauses; a cache thrash can cause transient inference stalls while the runtime rebuilds attention state.
- The affected requests were using the mid-sized variant with 6 concurrent streams; fallback routing introduced an extra queuing hop.
- Some of the chunked-transfer writes from the runtime to proxy were fragmented into unusually small frames (<256 bytes) which can trigger client-side reassembly delays.

Suggested mitigation to present to Avenir while we fix the root cause:
1) Temporarily pin them to the larger model variant (higher memory footprint, avoids eviction) for the remainder of the trial — we can credit them for the cost delta.
2) Turn off automatic fallback routing for their tenant to prevent queuing hops during bursts.
3) Configure client to use the non-chunked (single-response) path for stakeholder demos as Sergio suggested.

I can prepare a short executive summary for the renewal team with the cost/impact estimate.
— Markus
Runtime Reliability Lead

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@avenirhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live inference interruptions during demo — mitigation plan & exec ask

Alyssa — we dug in and have a confirmed remediation path. Short version: the runtime's cache eviction behavior, combined with automatic model-variant fallback, created a transient supply shock to the token producer which looked like "quiet windows" on your client.

What we propose right now (low friction):
- We will pin Avenir's tenant to the larger model variant for the next 7 days and disable fallback routing. This eliminates the eviction/queue hop path. We will apply a usage credit to offset the cost difference for the trial.
- For any customer-facing demos, use the single-response (non-streaming) endpoint; we’ll include a documentation note on how to do this from the Avenir SDK.
- Our engineering team will deliver a runtime patch to reduce small-frame fragmentation and improve write coalescing within 72 hours.

We propose a 30-minute executive sync tomorrow to review the fix, the credit, and the renewal touchpoints. Sergio — can you coordinate times with their stakeholders?

Attachments: SLA-summary-Avenir-2026-07.pdf (summary + proposed credit)

Thanks,
Grace
Director, Product Reliability

Next steps for commercial: Sergio, please confirm the credit details in the renewal thread and schedule the 30m sync for Monday morning. Hannah/Markus — please ship a short postmortem (SRE-style) and a permanent mitigation plan for avoiding eviction storms under the QA backlog.

Jordan
